description: A sixteen channel step sequencer of sixty-four steps per channel, where each channel can put out triggers, gates or voltages, with an Open Sound Control interface

params.text: Sets the tempo of the internal clock, from a quarter of the note value per minute up to sixty-four times it, and the reading above shows the result
Starts and stops playback, and the lamp on it shows whether the sequence is running
Sends playback back to the first step, and while playback is stopped arms step one for the next start
Sets how many steps the sequence plays before it returns to the first, 1 to 64
Picks which of the 64 patterns is played, which is the number under PATT on the left of the display
Picks which of the 64 patterns the pads and knobs are editing, which is the number under PATT on the right of the display
Picks which of the sixteen channels the pads and knobs are editing, 1 to 16, shown under CHNL and coloured to match that channel's output jack
Picks the output mode of the channel being edited, from TRIG, RTRG and GATE for pulses and gates through VOLT, NOTE and PATT for voltages
Copies the whole pattern being edited, all sixteen channels, to the clipboard
Copies the channel being edited, in the pattern being edited, to the clipboard
Pastes whatever was last copied into the pattern or channel being edited
Steps the clock division through 1/4, 1/8, 1/8T and 1/16, which changes what the tempo knob counts and is shown after BPM on the display
Turns the OSC connection on and saves the addresses and ports typed into the configuration screen
Switched on, the OSC connection is opened again whenever the patch is loaded
Shows and hides the OSC configuration screen, where the send and receive addresses and ports are typed
Shows and hides the song mode screen, where the list of patterns the song plays is set
Switched on, playback follows the list of patterns on the song mode screen instead of staying on one pattern
Sets how many entries of the song mode list are played before it returns to the first
Sets what that step of the channel being edited puts out; in the trigger modes it toggles the step on and off, and in the voltage modes it sets a value
Sets which pattern that place in the song mode list plays, 1 to 64

inputs.text: A rising edge here sets the tempo of the internal clock, -10V for the slowest setting and 10V for the fastest
A rising edge here advances the sequence one step and takes over from the internal clock while a cable is present
A rising edge here sends playback back to the first step
Sets how many steps the sequence plays, -10V for one step and 10V for 64
Picks which pattern is played, -10V for pattern 1 and 10V for pattern 64

outputs.text: Carries that channel's output, and the ring of light around the jack shows when that channel is firing

notes: the pads and knobs edit one channel of one pattern at a time, chosen by the CHNL knob and the PATT knob under EDIT; the PATT knob under PLAYBACK is the one that plays
each of the sixteen channels keeps its own output mode, so the MODE knob changes the mode of the channel being edited rather than of the whole module
dragging across the pads with the mouse held down toggles every pad the pointer passes over, which is the quickest way to draw or clear a run of steps
hovering a step and pressing the copy key copies that step, and the paste key pastes a step, row or column back; the same actions are on the step's own right-click menu
with nothing patched to the clock jack the module runs from its own clock at the tempo set by the tempo knob; patching a clock there takes that over
the six modes are shared out per channel, so one module can put gates on some outputs and pitches on others at the same time
menu: Initialize (Reset Channel Mode) — a heading over three items that clear steps and put the output mode back to its default
Current Edit Channel — clears the channel being edited in the pattern being edited
Current Edit Pattern — clears all sixteen channels of the pattern being edited
All Patterns — clears every channel of all 64 patterns
Initialize (Keep Channel Mode) — a heading over the same three items, which clear the steps but leave each channel's output mode alone
Random Options — a heading over the two randomisers below it
> All Steps Random — gives every step of the channel being edited a fresh random value
> Structured Random — randomises the channel being edited in a pattern rather than step by step
Set Value — on a step's own right-click menu, picks that step's value from a list instead of by dragging
Copy Step — on a step's own right-click menu, copies that step to the clipboard
Copy Row — on a step's own right-click menu, copies the whole row that step is in
Copy Column — on a step's own right-click menu, copies the whole column that step is in
Paste Step — on a step's own right-click menu, pastes a copied step here
Paste Row — on a step's own right-click menu, pastes a copied row starting here
Paste Column — on a step's own right-click menu, pastes a copied column starting here
Clear Clipboard — on a step's own right-click menu, throws away whatever was copied
Song Mode — clears the list of patterns the song plays, and appears only while song mode is available
Shift Values — a heading over the two items below it
> +1 V/Octave/Patt — raises every step by one volt, one octave or one pattern, over a submenu of Current Edit Channel, Current Edit Pattern or All Patterns
> -1 V/Octave/Patt — lowers every step by one volt, one octave or one pattern, over the same three choices

inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
